items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions Lionel Hampton, but the interviewee (Curtis Fuller) does not respond with any personal anecdote, memory, or statement regarding a relationship with Hampton.

ctx.x: Yeah. He had to be almost goated into it. We went up there. They know the difference between (Scats frenetic Al Grey solo) Al Grey. After a while you sit there and – oh jeez. The ladies leave like, “Ahhh!”

Do you think that was typical, I’m thinking of Lionel Hampton. I would go to Blues Alley and I’d see Lionel Hampton and I’d look at his audience. It was predictable: what would happen, who would do it. Meaning, women with their husbands, how they would react, they could create this night after night, after night.

I was so pleased, this last little two weeks in Italy. In Italy, I was just so pleased and I was also in Paris this time. I saw students, young students, just like in the club last night . [There were] at least 10 trombonists, and singers from the school here and young kids. I was really impressed with the students. I think the Kennedy Center going over and including Howard and redoing the Duke Ellington school is a good thing. We’ve got these kids they’re bringin’ in here from China and North Korea, South Korea…
